plan: 2 Chronicles 8:1-18; 1 Kings 9:15-28; 1 Kings 10:1-13; 2 Chronicles 9:1-12; 1 Kings 10:14-29; 2 Chronicles 9:13-28; 2 Chronicles 1:14-17

readings.title: The Covenant Renewed
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH appears to Solomon with a promise and a warning.
readings.text: [1 Kings 9:1] And it came to be, when Shelomoh had finished building <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign, and <dn>את</dn> all the desire of Shelomoh which he was pleased to do, [2] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh the second time, as <dn>He</dn> had appeared to him at Gib‛on. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, “<dq><dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> your prayer and <dn>את</dn> your supplication that you have made before <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> have set <dn>את</dn> this house apart which you have built to put <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name there forever, and <dn>My</dn> eyes and <dn>My</dn> heart shall always be there.</dq> [4] <dq>“And you, if you walk before <dn>Me</dn> as your father Daviḏ walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you, if you guard <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> right-rulings,</dq> [5] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of your reign over Yisra’ěl forever, as <dn>I</dn> promised Daviḏ your father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours on the throne of Yisra’ěl.’</dq> [6] <dq>“If you at all turn back, you or your sons, from following <dn>Me</dn>, and do not guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> commands, <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws, which <dn>I</dn> have set before you, but shall go and serve other mighty ones and bow yourselves to them,</dq> [7] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from the face of the soil which <dn>I</dn> have given them, and send away from <dn>My</dn> presence <dn>את</dn> this house which <dn>I</dn> have set apart for <dn>My</dn> Name. And Yisra’ěl shall be a proverb and a mockery among all the peoples.</dq> [8] <dq>“And this house, which has been exalted, everyone who passes by it shall be astonished, and hiss, and say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done thus to this land and to this house?’</dq> [9] <dq>“Then they shall say, ‘Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>את</dn> their fathers out of the land of Mitsrayim, and they took hold of other mighty ones, and bowed themselves to them and served them. That is why <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought <dn>את</dn> all this evil on them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Land of Kabul
readings.subtitle: Solomon's territorial exchange with Hiram of Tyre.
readings.text: [1 Kings 9:10] And it came to be, at the end of twenty years, that Shelomoh had built <dn>את</dn> the two houses, <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign. [11] Ḥiram the sovereign of Tsor had supplied <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh with cedar and cypress and gold, as much as he desired. Then Sovereign Shelomoh gave Ḥiram twenty cities in the land of Galil. [12] And Ḥiram came from Tsor to see <dn>את</dn> the cities which Shelomoh had given him, but they were not right in his eyes, [13] and he said, “What are these cities you have given me, my brother?” And he called them the land of Kaḇul, as they are to this day. [14] And Ḥiram sent the sovereign one hundred and twenty talents of gold.

readings.title: Solomon's Building Projects
readings.subtitle: The use of forced labor to construct cities and fortifications.
readings.text: [1 Kings 9:15] And this is the purpose of the compulsory labour which Sovereign Shelomoh raised, to build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> his own house, and <dn>את</dn> Millo, and <dn>את</dn> the wall of Yerushalayim, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥatsor, and <dn>את</dn> Meḡiddo, and <dn>את</dn> Gezer – [16] Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim had gone up and taken <dn>את</dn> Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites who dwelt in the city, and had given it as a payment for the bride to his daughter, Shelomoh’s wife – [17] and Shelomoh built <dn>את</dn> Gezer, and <dn>את</dn> Lower Běyth Ḥoron, [18] and <dn>את</dn> Ba‛alath, and <dn>את</dn> Tamar in the wilderness, in the land of Yehuḏah, [19] and <dn>את</dn> all the storage cities that Shelomoh had, and <dn>את</dn> cities for his chariots and <dn>את</dn> cities for his cavalry, and <dn>את</dn> whatever Shelomoh desired to build in Yerushalayim, and in Leḇanon, and in all the land of his rule. [20] All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Ḥittites, the Perizzites, the Ḥivvites, and the Yeḇusites, who were not of the children of Yisra’ěl – [21] their descendants who were left in the land after them, whom the children of Yisra’ěl had not been able to destroy completely – from these Shelomoh raised compulsory labour, as it is to this day. [22] But Shelomoh did not make slaves of the children of Yisra’ěl, because they were men of battle, and his servants, and his rulers, and his officers, and commanders of his chariots, and his cavalry. [23] These were the chiefs of the officials who were over the work of Shelomoh: five hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people who did the work.

readings.title: Worship, Trade, and the Navy
readings.subtitle: Solomon's religious observances and his naval expedition to Ophir.
readings.text: [1 Kings 9:24] But the daughter of Pharaoh came up from the City of Daviḏ to her house that he built for her. Then he built <dn>את</dn> Millo. [25] And three times a year Shelomoh brought ascending offerings and peace offerings on the slaughter-place which he had built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he burned incense with <dn>את</dn> that which was before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – thus gave completeness to the House. [26] And Sovereign Shelomoh built a fleet of ships at Etsyon Geḇer, which is near Ěyloth on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Eḏom. [27] And Ḥiram sent <dn>את</dn> his servants with the fleet, seamen who knew the sea, to work with the servants of Shelomoh. [28] And they went to Ophir, and took four hundred and twenty talents of gold from there, and brought it to Sovereign Shelomoh.

readings.title: The Queen of Sheba's Visit
readings.subtitle: Her journey to witness Solomon's wisdom and wealth.
readings.text: [1 Kings 10:1] And the sovereigness of Sheḇa heard of <dn>את</dn> the report of Shelomoh concerning the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and came to try him with hard questions. [2] And she came to Yerushalayim with a very great company, with camels that bore spices, very much gold, and precious stones. And she came to Shelomoh, and she spoke with <dn>את</dn> him about all that was in her heart. [3] And Shelomoh answered <dn>את</dn> all her questions. There was no matter hidden for the sovereign that he did not make known to her. [4] And the sovereigness of Sheḇa saw <dn>את</dn> all the wisdom of Shelomoh, and <dn>את</dn> the house that he had built, [5] and <dn>את</dn> the food on his table, and <dn>את</dn> the seating of his servants, and <dn>את</dn> the service of his waiters and their attire, and <dn>את</dn> his cupbearers, and <dn>את</dn> his ascending offerings which he offered in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and there was no more spirit in her. [6] Then she said to the sovereign, “The word I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom was true. [7] “But I did not believe the words until I came and saw with my own eyes. And see, I have not been told the half! Your wisdom and prosperity exceed the report which I heard. [8] “Blessed are your men and blessed are these your servants, who stand continually before you, who are hearing <dn>את</dn> your wisdom! [9] “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who delighted in you, to put you on the throne of Yisra’ěl! Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has loved <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl forever, therefore <dn>He</dn> made you sovereign, to do right-ruling and righteousness.” [10] And she gave the sovereign one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and very many spices, and precious stones. Never again did so many spices come as the sovereigness of Sheḇa gave to Sovereign Shelomoh. [11] And also, the ships of Ḥiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought almug wood, a great many, and precious stones from Ophir. [12] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> the almug wood steps for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for the sovereign’s house, also lyres and harps for singers. No such almug wood has come or been seen to this day. [13] And Sovereign Shelomoh gave the sovereigness of Sheḇa <dn>את</dn> all she desired, whatever she asked, besides what he gave her according to the hand of Sovereign Shelomoh. And she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.

readings.title: The Splendor of Solomon's Kingdom
readings.subtitle: An accounting of his immense annual income and luxurious possessions.
readings.text: [1 Kings 10:14] And the weight of gold that came to Shelomoh yearly was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold, [15] besides that from men of travel, and the profit from traders, and from all the sovereigns of Araḇia, and from the governors of the land. [16] And Sovereign Shelomoh made two hundred large shields of beaten gold – six hundred pieces of gold went into each shield; [17] and three hundred shields of beaten gold – three minas of gold went into each shield. And the sovereign put them in the House of the Forest of Leḇanon. [18] And the sovereign made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with refined gold. [19] The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round at the back, and there were armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the armrests. [20] And twelve lions were standing there, one on each side of the six steps. The like of it was never made in any reign. [21] And all the drinking vessels of Sovereign Shelomoh were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Leḇanon were of refined gold – not of silver, for this was reckoned of little value in the days of Shelomoh. [22] For the sovereign had ships of Tarshish at sea with the fleet of Ḥiram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish came bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and baboons.

readings.title: Solomon's International Influence
readings.subtitle: His fame, military might, and extensive trade in horses and chariots.
readings.text: [1 Kings 10:23] And Sovereign Shelomoh was greater than any of the sovereigns of the earth in riches and wisdom. [24] And all the earth sought <dn>את</dn> the presence of Shelomoh to hear his wisdom, which <dn>Elohim</dn> had put in his heart. [25] And they were each bringing his present: objects of silver and objects of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, the matter of a year by year. [26] And Shelomoh gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the sovereign in Yerushalayim. [27] And the sovereign made <dn>את</dn> silver as common in Yerushalayim as stones, and he made <dn>את</dn> cedars as plenty as the sycamores which are in the low country. [28] And Shelomoh had horses brought out from Mitsrayim and Quěh; the sovereign’s merchants bought them in Quěh at a price. [29] And a chariot came up and went out from Mitsrayim for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse one hundred and fifty. And so, by their hand, they brought them out to all the sovereigns of the Ḥittites and the sovereigns of Aram.
